subject: significance testing for densities with unequal variance

messages.author: c977cac854060e86
messages.subject: significance testing for densities with unequal variance
parts:
Hello,

I want to compare two stratum densities that have separate detection
probability estimates. The degrees of freedom are close (34 and 35) so tha=
t
is not a problem. But the variances are very different (.8379 and .170)
and the %cv for both is well over 20% (.6001 and .5998). So should I use a=
n
unequal variance t test from Moser and Stevens (1992), and should I log
transform my densities and use cv^2 instead of the variance in my t test? =
I
could not find anything about this in the Introduction to Distance Sampling
book besides the basic hypothesis testing with equal variances (p85), so is
this refered to in the Advanced Distance Sampling? Thank you.

Moser BK, S*t*evens GR. 1992. Homogenei*t*y of variance in *t*he *t*wo-*
sample* means *t*es*t*. Am S*t*a*t* 46:19=9621.
